alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The cochlear duct is the portion of the membranous labyrinth located in the cochlea. Its location is intermediary between the scala vestibuli above and the scala tympani below. The cochlear duct houses the receptor for sound, the organ of Corti.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT: In the adult, bipolar neurons are found in organs of special sense, such as this spiral ganglion located in the cochlea. A dendrite originates in the organ of Corti and extends to the cell body of a bipolar neuron; from there, an axon emerges to form the cochlear division of cranial nerve VIII.

alternativas.feedback: The tectorial membrane rests on the hair cells of the organ of Corti. Stereocilia of the hair cells are embedded in this membrane. Deflection of hair cells creates a shearing force between the stereocilia and the tectorial membrane, initiating a neural impulse.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Stria vascularis, along with related cells in the maculae and cristae ampullares, produces endolymph. The stria vascularis, an epithelium located on the outer wall of the cochlear duct, is unique in that it is the only vascularized epitheliium in mammals.
